text.title: Process Mining and Intelligent Automation Analysis Failure Modes
text.summary: Antipatterns observed in real engagements applying process-mining-automation. Each entry pairs symptom + root cause + fix.

antipattern.symptom: Building as-is from interviews when logs exist.
antipattern.fix: Use event logs as source of truth; interviews for context only.
Conformance-check is mandatory; without it, deviations stay hidden.

antipattern.symptom: Picking automation candidates by loudest voice.
antipattern.fix: Lock scoring matrix before review; objective ranking only.

antipattern.symptom: Verdict defaults to RPA regardless of variance.
antipattern.fix: High-variance processes need orchestration or AI-assist, not brittle RPA scripts.

antipattern.symptom: Automating a high-volume process before checking for standardization — discovering mid-project that 40% of cases are exceptions.
antipattern.root-cause: Volume alone is not a sufficient criterion. A 1,000-transaction/day process with 50% exceptions requires human judgment more than automation; scoring all six criteria prevents this failure.
antipattern.fix: Score all six criteria (six-criterion-scoring-matrix) before committing; an exception rate above the standardization threshold routes to process improvement first.

antipattern.symptom: Selecting automation vendor before completing the process assessment — vendor locks in architecture before requirements are known.
antipattern.root-cause: Complete the assessment matrix and determine whether RPA or intelligent automation applies before engaging vendors; the tool selection follows from the process characteristics, not from the vendor relationship.
antipattern.fix: Finish the scoring matrix and the RPA-vs-intelligent-automation call (rpa-vs-intelligent-automation) first; only then shortlist vendors.
